papers.summary: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.
papers.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems

papers.summary: The CHQ model describes viscoelastic phase separation in a polymer--solvent mixture: a Cahn--Hilliard equation for the polymer volume fraction $φ$ is two-way coupled, through a phase-dependent cross-diffusion flux, to a damped relaxation equation for a scalar bulk elastic stress $q$. We propose a scalar-auxiliary-variable (SAV) time discretisation of this system, combining the SAV reformulation of the double-well potential with a second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) and a second-order extrapolation of all phase-dependent mobilities: a linear, computationally cheaper complement to the reference scheme's fully nonlinear Newton solve. The resulting method is (i) linear at every time step, with a coupling structure we prove has exactly one solution at every step, for every choice of time-step size; (ii) mass conserving, exactly, as an algebraic identity of the discrete equations themselves (the only drift ever seen numerically traces to the finite tolerance of the iterative linear solver, not a failure of the conservation property); and (iii) unconditionally stable for a modified discrete energy, via an exact one-step energy--dissipation identity. We show the energy identity extends to this filtered variant as well, with two explicit extra non-negative terms. Hence, the scheme actually producing the physics results is itself provably stable for the same energy. A Fourier--Galerkin implementation verifies that the energy identity holds at every time step to within floating-point round-off. It also confirms second-order temporal accuracy, including in the steep-interface regime, and agreement with an independently implemented nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver. Compared with that independent nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver, at equal grid resolution, the SAV method uses $2.5$--$3.0\times$ fewer linear-solver iterations and $1.7$--$2.0\times$ less wall-clock time.
papers.title: A linear, second-order, unconditionally energy-stable scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme for the CHQ viscoelastic phase-separation model

papers.summary: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration. For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.
papers.title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster

papers.summary: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.
papers.title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices

papers.summary: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $ω_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $ω_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $ω_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $ω_\mathbb{F}$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.
papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers

papers.summary: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\barω_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\barω_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.
papers.title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system

papers.summary: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schrödinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.
papers.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

papers.summary: We construct a bounded Borel set in the plane whose orthogonal projection onto every line is non-Borel. This gives a negative answer to a question of Thierry De Pauw.
papers.title: A bounded Borel set in the plane none of whose orthogonal projections is Borel

papers.summary: In this short note, we develop a duality-based, purely operator-theoretic method for proving several classical maximal inequalities on $L^p$ spaces for $p\in(1,\infty)$. The method applies to maximal ergodic operators, Hardy--Littlewood maximal functions, and maximal Radon averaging operators, and derives their boundedness directly from structural properties of the underlying operators. Further, we show that the same duality principle extends beyond maximal functions. We develop a theory of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for sequences of bounded positive monotone operators on Hilbert spaces, using soft arguments that apply to various classical operators in analysis. In particular, answering a question that had been open for some time, we give direct proofs of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for convolution operators associated with lacunary dilations of smooth bumps on $\mathbb R^d$, completely avoiding any appeal to martingale inequalities.
papers.title: Duality in Harmonic Analysis and beyond

papers.summary: This paper studies doctrines in categorical logic and their relations to fragments of geometric logic. After a brief account of the historical context for the notion of doctrine in categorical logic, we propose our working definition. We then show that there is a Galois connection between the poset of doctrines and the poset of fragments of geometric logic as defined in the framework of Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi, recently developed by the first and third authors. Concretely, the connection is realised by a general construction of syntactic categories and classifying topoi which encompasses all well-known examples in categorical logic. This yields a mirror symmetry, between the algebraic world of doctrines and the geometric world of topoi: to provide evidence of this phenomenon, we prove a few symmetric results relating doctrines and logics by means of syntactic categories and classifying topoi. We conclude with a discussion on the theme of conceptual completeness.
papers.title: Logic vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry

papers.summary: We study the countable partition model over a set of atoms of arbitrary uncountable cardinality $κ$. Its supports are partitions of the atoms into countably many blocks, and a permutation fixes a support when it preserves each block setwise. This model was proposed by Bruce and studied by Banerjee. We prove that dependent choice holds for every $κ$, although the filter of subgroups is not closed under countable intersections. Choice for well-orderable families holds exactly when $κ<\aleph_{ω_1}$; when $κ\ge\aleph_{ω_1}$, an $ω_1$-indexed family witnesses its failure. The Hartogs and Lindenbaum numbers of the set of atoms are both $ω_1$. The proofs use permutations matching blocks of equal cardinality and establish shift completeness of the filter. Together with Banerjee's failure of $\mathsf{DC}_{ω_1}$, these results determine which dependent choice principles hold in the model.
papers.title: Choice principles in countable partition models

papers.summary: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.
papers.title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem

papers.summary: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.
papers.title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings

papers.summary: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{ξ\in \mathbb F_q^d:ξ_1^2+\cdots+ξ_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, dσ)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $η_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $η_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
papers.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions

papers.summary: Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case. As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian Čech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.
papers.title: Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers

papers.summary: We introduce a $q$-analog of the one-variable middle Laplace transform defined by the first author. We establish its invertibility and preservation of irreducibility, and derive a decomposition of $q$-middle convolution in terms of this transform. As applications, we obtain integral representations of solutions to the confluent $q$-hypergeometric equation and its variant, and construct a transformation of the $2\times 2$ Lax linear equation associated with the $q$-Painlevé equation of type $A_4^{(1)}$.
papers.title: $q$-middle Laplace transform and its applications

papers.summary: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincaré polynomial is nonzero.
papers.title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras

papers.summary: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials

papers.summary: Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $ω$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $ω$-chains. We then introduce the lifting property for posets with no maximal element and show that a poset can be partitioned into $ω$-chains if and only if it has the lifting property.
papers.title: General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $ω$-Chains

papers.summary: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.
papers.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
